name: Crypto / web3 wallet risk scoring & on-chain transaction monitoring
category: New — on-chain risk and AML for crypto
parent_research_topic: Beava use cases — current and potential applications of beava as a real-time feature server

domain_fit.domain_name: Crypto wallet risk scoring and on-chain transaction monitoring for VASPs, wallet providers, and DeFi protocols
domain_fit.one_line_definition: A crypto exchange, wallet provider, or DeFi protocol's risk / compliance / fraud engine must, within ~100–500 ms of a deposit, withdrawal, swap, or wallet-connect event, score the originating and beneficiary address against rolling behavioural features and direct/indirect exposure to sanctioned, mixer, scam, or hack-tainted addresses, so the platform can block, hold, freeze, alert, or warn the user before the asset moves on-chain.
domain_fit.representative_jobs_to_be_done: 1) Score every deposit/withdrawal/swap in real time against the originating address's rolling inbound/outbound velocity, sudden mixer/CEX interaction, hop-distance to sanctioned and Tornado-Cash-tainted addresses, and the customer's own historical baseline, so withdrawals can be auto-held or sanctions deposits frozen before settlement on-chain. 2) Generate Travel-Rule-driven and SAR-driven alerts (structuring, peel-chains, dormant-wake, rapid in/out, sudden cross-jurisdiction corridor, RMT/money-mule clusters) for the compliance case manager, with feature values that are reproducible at audit time. 3) Compute per-(customer, deposit_address) peer-network features (counterparty fan-in, peer-address co-clustering with known mules / scam addresses) used by ML scorers and graph engines to flag illicit-cluster membership before the address builds a track record. 4) Surface in-wallet transaction-risk warnings ('this address has 1-hop exposure to OFAC-sanctioned Tornado Cash, do you still want to sign?') for wallet providers and dApps via a sub-100 ms feature lookup at signing time.
domain_fit.event_shapes: On-chain events ingested from node providers (Alchemy, QuickNode, Infura, Helius, Bitquery, in-house archive node + mempool firehose) and L2 indexers: deposit_observed (tx_hash, chain_id, block_height, from_address, to_address, asset, amount, timestamp, source_label?), withdrawal_initiated, withdrawal_confirmed, address_first_seen, mempool_pending_tx. Off-chain events from the exchange/wallet/dApp: fiat_on_ramp (customer_id, fiat_amount, payment_method, KYC_tier), fiat_off_ramp, internal_transfer (customer-to-customer), order_filled (matched-trade, taker/maker, asset_pair), dex_swap (pool, in_asset, out_asset, slippage), wallet_connect (dApp_origin, signer_address), transaction_sign_request (address, calldata, value, chain_id, dApp). Risk-update events from third parties: chainalysis_address_label_update, trm_risk_score_update, ofac_sdn_list_update, scam_db_update. Common fields: timestamp, customer_id (where known), address, chain_id, asset, amount, USD_value_at_ts, counterparty_address, counterparty_label, channel, country (from IP/KYC), KYC_risk_tier, sanctions_status, exposure_category.
domain_fit.feature_shapes: Per-address rolling counters and sums: count(inbound_tx, window=1h/24h/7d/30d), count(outbound_tx, window), sum(inbound_USD, window), sum(outbound_USD, window), velocity (tx/min, tx/h), max(amount, window), avg(amount, window). Distinct cardinalities: count(distinct_counterparty, 24h/7d/30d) — HLL acceptable beyond 24h. First-seen / dormant-wake: time_since_first_seen, time_since_last_outbound, is_first_outbound_to_high_risk_jurisdiction, age_at_first_high_value_send. Hop-distance / exposure features: min_hop_to_OFAC_address, min_hop_to_known_mixer (Tornado Cash, Sinbad, Wasabi, JoinMarket, Railgun), min_hop_to_known_hack_pool, indirect_exposure_USD_within_k_hops, %_volume_from_high_risk_counterparties. Mixer / CEX / DEX interaction flags: ever_received_from_mixer_30d, time_since_last_mixer_interaction, sudden_CEX_deposit (large send to CEX after long dormancy), sudden_bridge_use. Peer-network features: count(peer_addresses_co_clustered_with_known_mules), peer_group_z_score for amount and velocity. Structuring / peel-chain heuristics: count(outbound < $10k threshold, 7d), ratio(below_threshold/total), fan-out distinct sinks 24h, fan-in distinct sources 24h. Distributions: amount t-digest per address, hour-of-day percentile, asset-mix Shannon entropy. Per-customer aggregates: sum(USD_volume across all owned addresses, 24h/7d/30d), distinct_chains_touched, distinct_high_risk_jurisdictions. Windows are predominantly sliding (1m / 1h / 24h / 7d / 30d / 90d), tumbling calendar-day for CTR-style aggregation, and 'session' = per-trading-session for behavioural baselines.
domain_fit.entity_grain: Multiple parallel grains. Primary: (address, chain_id) — the natural on-chain key, explosive cardinality (100M–1B+ addresses). Secondary: (customer_id) — the regulator-facing entity, bounded by KYC. Tertiary: (customer_id, deposit_address) — the customer-to-address mapping (one customer often owns many addresses). Cross-pair grains: (from_address, to_address) and (customer, counterparty_address) for pair-level structuring and pass-through detection. Cluster grain: (cluster_id) where addresses have been resolved into entities by Chainalysis/TRM/Elliptic. For wallet providers and DeFi: (signer_address, dApp_origin) at signing time. For DEX/AMM-level monitoring: (pool_address, signer_address).
domain_fit.window_semantics_required: Predominantly sliding windows over short-to-medium horizons (1m, 5m, 1h, 24h, 7d, 30d) for velocity, mixer-interaction recency, peel-chain detection. Hopping windows (e.g. 30d hopping by 1d) for peer-group baselines. Calendar-day tumbling for FinCEN $3k Travel-Rule thresholds and $10k CTR-equivalent reporting. Session windows are useful at the (customer, trading-session) grain. Approximate sketches (HLL for distinct-counterparty, CMS for heavy-hitter counterparties, t-digest for amount quantiles) are acceptable for all behavioural features; exact counts and sums are required only for regulator-bound thresholds (Travel-Rule USD$3k for FinCEN, EUR$1k FATF baseline, EU TFR with no minimum for CASP-to-CASP). On-chain primitive exposure (k-hop to OFAC) is naturally a graph query rather than a window, but the cached hop-distance can be served as a feature.
domain_fit.exactly_once_or_idempotency_needs: Strict idempotency required. Chain re-orgs (Ethereum 1–2 block, Bitcoin 6-block) cause the same tx_hash to be re-emitted; mempool-then-confirmed pipelines double-publish; node providers replay on reconnect. Re-publishing the same on-chain event must not double-count a velocity counter, double-count a Travel-Rule aggregate, or double-trigger an alert. Dedupe key is typically (tx_hash, log_index, chain_id) for on-chain events and end_to_end_id for off-chain. Re-org handling additionally requires the feature store to support tombstone / compensating-write semantics, which is a non-trivial addition beyond simple at-least-once dedupe.

technical_fit.latency_budget: Tight. Public vendor positioning: TRM Wallet Screening API <300 ms (June 2025 product update, previously <400 ms) and Elliptic Holistic sub-second across 2B+ labeled addresses. For at-signing transaction warnings in wallets (MetaMask + Blockaid, Phantom), the end-to-end budget is ~200–500 ms because the user is staring at the modal; the wallet's own UI overhead consumes most of that. For exchange withdrawal hold and DEX-routing risk checks, the budget is typically 100–500 ms p99. Beava's sub-millisecond TCP get / batch_get is far inside any of these budgets and would mostly be limited by upstream chain ingestion latency.
technical_fit.feature_freshness_sla: Mixed and event-type-dependent. Per-address velocity counters and mixer-interaction flags should reflect the just-arrived tx (effective freshness ~0 ms, atomic update-and-read). Hop-distance and cluster-membership features can tolerate seconds-to-minutes of staleness because they depend on heavy graph computation off-line. Sanctions-list joins must refresh on every OFAC SDN update (typically daily, sometimes intra-day). Peer-group baselines can tolerate hours. Behavioural baselines (90d): nightly recompute. Travel-Rule aggregates: same-day exact.
technical_fit.throughput_profile: Heterogeneous and chain-dependent. A mid-tier exchange might see 100–1,000 EPS of on-chain + off-chain events; a top-tier exchange (Binance, Coinbase, OKX with USD ~$5.5B daily spot + ~$40B derivatives) sees thousands-to-tens-of-thousands EPS across all chains and events; Solidus Labs' HALO platform reports monitoring 'over one trillion events per day' across centralised + decentralised venues (~11.5M EPS aggregate); Chainalysis maps >1B addresses and serves 9 of top-10 exchanges; Elliptic reports >2M screenings/month with sub-second 'Holistic' latency. Beava's published ~684k EPS on a single Apple-M4 core (TCP+msgpack, parallel=16) is comfortably above any single-tenant exchange's steady-state and leaves ample headroom for 20–100 feature reads per decision. [uncertain] — per-buyer EPS for specific exchanges and wallet providers is not publicly disclosed.
technical_fit.read_to_write_ratio: Read-heavy. Each on-chain event is one write but every wallet-connect, every signing modal, every order-pre-check, and every withdrawal-pre-check fans out into 20–80+ feature reads across rules, ML scorer, and case-management dashboards. Wallet-provider use cases (in-wallet transaction warnings) are extremely read-heavy because most warnings never trigger a write. Reads dominate writes by roughly 20–100x.
technical_fit.state_size_estimate: Large and explosive. Address-grain cardinality is essentially unbounded; Ethereum alone has >300M unique addresses cumulatively, ~24M+ active wallets across all chains daily (DappRadar Q2 2025), 40M+ smart accounts deployed on EVM L2s. A top exchange tracking deposit/withdrawal addresses plus seen-counterparties realistically holds 100M–1B+ active address records. At ~2–8 KB per-address state (multi-window counters, distinct-counterparty HLL, amount t-digest, mixer-interaction flags, hop-distance cache, cluster_id pointer), the working set is 200 GB–8 TB. Beava's in-memory-only single-node model fits a mid-tier exchange's hot working set on a beefy node but exceeds single-node RAM for top-tier exchanges and serious wallet providers; sharding or tiered storage (RAM → SSD) is needed. [uncertain] — bytes/address is an order-of-magnitude planning estimate.
technical_fit.cardinality_pattern: Explosive at the address grain (100M–1B+, unbounded), slowly-growing at the customer grain (bounded by KYC at typically 1M–100M per exchange), small and bounded at cluster/entity grain (Chainalysis labels millions of entities, but the active hot-set is far smaller). Counterparty-pair cardinality is explosive in the long tail. Mixer/sanctioned-address lists are small and bounded (OFAC SDN ~50k entries, mixer pool addresses in the thousands). Country-corridor: small.
technical_fit.typical_state_lifecycle_and_ttl: Medium-to-long. Short-window velocity counters (1m/1h/24h): minutes-to-hours TTL. Velocity (7d/30d) and mixer-interaction features: 30–90 days. Behavioural baselines: 90–180 days. Dormant-wake detection: 365+ days (regulators care about long-dormant addresses suddenly active). Travel-Rule reporting retention (FATF / FinCEN / EU TFR): 5 years for supporting documentation (handled by archive, not the live feature store). KYC linkage state lives years. Hot address tail is long because most addresses go quiet but cannot safely be evicted while customer relationships persist.
technical_fit.typical_feature_count_per_decision: 30–150 per decision. Real-time deposit/withdrawal screening typically queries: 6–10 velocity counters across multiple windows, 4–8 mixer/CEX/bridge flags, 3–6 hop-distance / exposure features, 5–10 peer-group z-scores, 4–8 cluster / counterparty labels, plus customer-grain aggregates. Investigator case-review re-fetches a larger vector. batch_get / pipelined reads are essential.
technical_fit.durability_requirements: Regulator-grade for exchanges, EMI-grade for wallet providers, best-effort for analytics tooling. Crypto VASPs under FATF R.16 / FinCEN / EU TFR / MiCA / MAS PSN02 / FCA / FINTRAC PCMLTFA are all required to retain Travel-Rule and SAR supporting evidence for 5+ years (system-of-record archive, not the live feature store). Beava's WAL + periodic snapshot is crash-safe enough for the derived-feature serving tier but does not satisfy archival retention; the upstream chain firehose + decision log archive does. The 'refuse on network-FS' default is the right guardrail for an exchange operator. Regulators (especially under EU AMLR / MiCA technical standards) will expect reproducibility: 'what was hop_distance_to_OFAC for address X at 14:32:07Z on 2026-02-14?' must be answerable.
technical_fit.deployment_topology_fit: Single-binary-per-region is workable for a mid-tier exchange or wallet provider. Top-tier exchanges (Binance, Coinbase, Kraken, OKX, Bybit) and global wallet providers (MetaMask serves >30M monthly active users) need multi-region active-active for global low-latency wallet-warning UX and for data-residency (EU MiCA / TFR push EU-customer data EU-resident); beava does not natively provide multi-region active-active in v0. Sidecar-to-existing-blockchain-intelligence-platform (TRM, Chainalysis, Elliptic, Merkle Science, Crystal, Scorechain, Solidus Labs HALO) is a realistic adoption path — beava becomes the low-latency derived-feature substrate that joins the third-party risk labels with the exchange's own per-customer behavioural state. Beava's lack of in-process sharding is a hard cap for top-tier exchanges given address-grain cardinality.

commercial_fit.who_buys: 1) Compliance / financial-crime / fraud engineering teams inside centralised crypto exchanges (Coinbase, Binance, Kraken, Bybit, OKX, Bitget, Crypto.com, Bitstamp, Gemini), 2) wallet providers (MetaMask/ConsenSys, Phantom, Rabby, Trust Wallet, Coinbase Wallet, Ledger Live, OKX Wallet), 3) DeFi protocols and DEX aggregators (Uniswap, 1inch, CowSwap, Aave, Compound) under MiCA + emerging US frameworks, 4) Web3 dApps and on/off-ramp providers (MoonPay, Ramp, Transak, Banxa), 5) institutional custodians and prime brokers (Fireblocks, BitGo, Anchorage, Copper), 6) Travel-Rule solution providers (Notabene, Sumsub, 21 Analytics, Veriscope) embedding feature substrates, 7) regtech vendors themselves (TRM, Chainalysis, Elliptic, Merkle Science, Crystal, Scorechain, Solidus Labs, Nominis) who might embed beava as the low-latency substrate underneath their UI. Budget owners: MLRO / Chief Compliance Officer; engineering owns the build.
commercial_fit.market_size_signal: Large and structurally regulator-pulled. The global cryptocurrency AML market is sized at USD ~1.2B in 2025 growing to USD ~4.8B by 2034 (Intel Market Research / 16.5% CAGR); the broader blockchain-analytics + crypto-compliance market reached USD ~4.41B in 2025 (Chainalysis market data). TRM Labs achieved unicorn status with a $1B valuation and $220M total funding (Feb 2026 Series C $70M). Chainalysis serves 9 of top-10 crypto exchanges, maps >1B addresses, holds ~45% of law-enforcement-user share globally. Elliptic reports 2M+ screenings/month and 2B+ labeled addresses. Solidus Labs HALO platform protects 25M+ retail+institutional investors and processes 1T+ events/day. Enforcement is enormous and accelerating: OKX paid $504M penalty (Feb 2025) for AML / MSB violations; Paxful $3.5M penalty (Dec 2025); Bybit suffered $1.5B hack (largest in history) driving regulator attention. [uncertain] — individual vendor revenues are not publicly disclosed.
commercial_fit.urgency_drivers: 1) EU MiCA fully in force from December 30, 2024 — every CASP needs production-grade transaction monitoring + Travel Rule + market-abuse surveillance. EBA Travel Rule Guidelines (July 2024) apply Dec 30 2024 with no threshold for CASP-to-CASP. 2) FATF Travel Rule — by mid-2025, 99 jurisdictions had passed or are advancing legislation; 85 of 117 (73%) have it on the books. France issued 14 enforcement notices Q4 2025; BaFin blocked 6 offshore exchanges; Philippines SEC targeting OKX/Bybit/Bitget. 3) Headline enforcement: OKX $504M (Feb 2025), Paxful $3.5M (Dec 2025), prior Binance $4.3B and BitMEX consent orders. 4) Bybit's $1.5B Lazarus-Group hack (Feb 2025) and the resulting trace-through-OKX-DEX $100M laundering chase put on-chain real-time monitoring on every exchange's CEO agenda. 5) US FinCEN August 2025 CVC-kiosk Notice + 2024 Travel-Rule $3k threshold + 2028 RIA AML obligations expand the buyer cohort. 6) Hack-related real-time response (frozen-deposit obligations, Lazarus-pattern detection) demands sub-second latency now, not minutes. 7) Wallet-provider competitive UX: MetaMask + Blockaid, Phantom + Blockaid set the bar for in-wallet warnings, forcing every wallet to add transaction-risk feature lookups. 8) EU AMLR / AMLA (applies 10 July 2027) brings crypto VASPs fully into the broader AML supervisory regime.
commercial_fit.regulatory_or_audit_constraints: Heavy. FATF R.16 (Travel Rule, USD/EUR $1k baseline). EU: MiCA (fully in force Dec 30 2024), EU TFR / Regulation 2023/1113 (no minimum for CASP-to-CASP, EBA Travel Rule Guidelines apply Dec 30 2024), GDPR. US: BSA / 31 CFR 1010.410(f) Travel Rule (FinCEN expanded to $3k for crypto in 2024), FinCEN MSB registration (Paxful precedent Dec 2025), OFAC sanctions screening, FinCEN SAR ($2k crypto threshold per FIN-2019-A003), state-by-state MTL, NYDFS Part 200. UK: FCA crypto registration regime, MLR 2017 + Travel Rule. Singapore MAS PSN02 + Travel Rule. Hong Kong SFC + AMLO. Canada FINTRAC + PCMLTFA. South Korea FIU + ISMS. Japan FSA + JVCEA. Australia AUSTRAC. UAE VARA. All push toward: (i) reproducible feature values at decision time, (ii) immutable audit log, (iii) 5-year retention, (iv) data-residency, (v) per-transfer originator/beneficiary attribution. Note: in many jurisdictions there is structural tension between GDPR right-to-erasure and the immutability of on-chain transactions.
commercial_fit.time_to_value_signal: Fast for prototype, slow for production cutover. 1–2 weeks for a wallet-velocity + mixer-flag + hop-distance demo against public datasets (Elliptic Bitcoin dataset, public Etherscan API, OFAC SDN list) and a synthetic event stream. 1–3 months for a shadow-mode deployment alongside a third-party risk feed (TRM/Chainalysis/Elliptic) computing per-customer behavioural baselines and per-address velocity. 6–12 months for regulator-grade production cutover (MiCA-aligned, FATF Travel Rule integrated, MLRO / Chief Compliance Officer sign-off, model validation, SOC2 / ISO 27001, runbook for WAL+snapshot recovery, multi-region failover). Crypto buyers' procurement cycles are faster than banks' (smaller, less bureaucratic) but the compliance bar is rising sharply post-OKX/Binance/Paxful enforcement. Apache-2.0 with no open-core is attractive to wallet providers and DeFi protocols that resist SaaS lock-in.

competition.incumbents: Generic streaming / feature-store stacks already deployed under crypto monitoring today: Apache Kafka + Flink (dual-pipeline architecture: Public Chain → Node Collector → Go/Rust service → Redis/Postgres for sub-second; Public Chain → Kafka → Flink → VeloDB for 1–3 s deep analytics — as documented in VeloDB / Apache Doris case studies for a top exchange with 80M+ users); Redis Enterprise as the low-latency feature cache; ClickHouse / VeloDB / Apache Doris / Druid for warm aggregates; Aerospike for sub-ms feature serving; Confluent for managed Kafka + on-chain stream ingestion; Tecton, Feast, Hopsworks, Fennel, Chalk as ML feature stores. Indexing layer: The Graph, Goldsky, SubQuery, Bitquery, Allium, Dune, Footprint. Open-source: Marble (open-source real-time decision engine for fraud/AML), Jube (AGPLv3 in-memory real-time AML+fraud). The dominant production pattern is 'Node firehose → Kafka → Flink + Redis + scoring engine + third-party risk API → case management UI'.
competition.competitive_incumbent_per_domain: Tier-1 blockchain intelligence: Chainalysis (KYT / Reactor / Storyline / Address Screening; 9 of top-10 exchanges; >1B addresses; ~45% LE share), TRM Labs (Wallet Screening <300ms p50, Transaction Monitoring, BLOCKINT API, 100+ chains, 29+ blockchains screened, 70M+ digital assets; $1B valuation, $220M raised), Elliptic (Lens, Holistic sub-second, Investigator; 2B+ labeled addresses, 2M+ screenings/month), Merkle Science (Compass real-time monitoring, predictive behaviour-based), Crystal (Crystal Expert / Crystal Lite; law-enforcement-heavy), Scorechain (250+ institutions, 40+ countries, EU-focused), Bitquery (data API), Allium (on-chain warehouse). Crypto-native AML / market-surveillance: Solidus Labs HALO (50+ market-abuse typologies, 1T+ events/day, BitMEX integration), Nominis, CryptoPolice, AnChain.AI. Travel-Rule providers: Notabene, Sumsub Crypto, 21 Analytics, Veriscope, Shyft. AML / fraud platforms targeting crypto: Sardine ($70M Series C, behavioural biometrics + crypto), Unit21 (<250 ms per-tx decision, crypto vertical, Uphold customer), Hawk (Hawk.AI, 150ms avg, crypto + fiat), Flagright (sub-300ms), ComplyAdvantage Mesh, Lucinity, Castellum.AI. In-wallet warning providers: Blockaid (MetaMask + Phantom default), Forta, Wallet Guard. Beava would slot underneath one of these as the feature substrate; it does not replace the chain-intelligence labels, the case manager, the Travel-Rule messaging, the SDN list, or the graph engine.
competition.beava_differentiator: 1) Single-binary, Apache-2.0, no broker / no ETL — attractive to wallet providers and DeFi protocols that resist SaaS lock-in and to mid-tier exchanges that today stitch Kafka+Flink+Redis+TRM/Chainalysis under their UI. 2) Declarative @bv.event / @bv.table primitives express address velocity, mixer-interaction flags, peer-group z-score, fan-in/fan-out as schema rather than Flink jobs + Lua scripts. 3) ~684k EPS on a single core gives huge headroom for the 100–500 EPS steady-state of a mid-tier exchange and supports the 30–150 feature reads per decision plus wallet-warning read amplification. 4) Sub-ms TCP get / batch_get is inside any wallet-warning, exchange-withdrawal, or DEX-pre-trade budget by an order of magnitude. 5) Atomic per-event update-and-read fits the rule 'this deposit must update the address's velocity counter before being scored against the mixer-recency threshold'. 6) HTTP/JSON + framed TCP (JSON or msgpack) lets a Rust/Go node firehose, a Python compliance scorer, or a TypeScript wallet warning UI all call beava directly. 7) WAL + snapshot with refuse-on-network-FS is the right default for a buyer who would otherwise quietly run on EFS and break crash recovery. 8) No open-core means embedding inside a third-party regtech vendor's product is licence-clean.
competition.where_beava_loses_today: 1) No TLS — disqualifying for any regulated VASP without an in-front mTLS-terminating proxy; even with one, exchange security teams want mTLS to the feature store. 2) No authn/authz / RBAC — every regulated buyer needs per-tenant tokens, per-role access, per-team audit. 3) No in-process sharding — caps single-tenant scale at one node; address-grain cardinality (100M–1B+) is the hardest single-node-RAM limit of any beava use case. 4) No hot-standby / replication — losing 90–365-day behavioural baselines on a crash is unacceptable to MLROs. 5) In-memory only — address-grain working set exceeds single-node RAM at top-tier exchanges; tiered storage (RAM → SSD) is needed. 6) No native point-in-time / as-of read — regulators under MiCA / FATF / FinCEN expect reproducibility of decision-time feature values. 7) No native on-chain risk-label integration (OFAC SDN, mixer lists, scam DB, Chainalysis/TRM/Elliptic webhooks) — every competitor ships this and many label vendors charge per-call. 8) No graph / hop-distance primitive — the hop-to-OFAC-or-mixer feature, which is the most-asked feature in this domain, currently requires offline graph computation cached as a key-value lookup; beava has no native graph layer. 9) No re-org / tombstone handling for chain reorganisations — a serious correctness issue. 10) No case-management UI / no SAR-narrative generator / no Travel-Rule messaging. 11) No triggers / no webhook on threshold-cross — exchange compliance teams want 'fire when min_hop_to_OFAC <= 1 OR sum(outbound_to_mixer, 24h) > $10k'. 12) No multi-tenancy — wallet-provider and regtech-vendor SaaS embedding needs per-tenant namespaces. 13) No native idempotency keys on push — required for at-least-once node firehoses to avoid double-counting velocity and Travel-Rule aggregates. 14) No data-residency controls — MiCA + GDPR require EU customer data on EU RAM. 15) No native chain re-org compensating-write semantics.
competition.integration_surface: Upstream producers: Ethereum / L2 archive nodes via JSON-RPC (geth, erigon, nethermind, reth), Bitcoin Core RPC, Solana RPC (Helius, Triton), node-as-a-service providers (Alchemy, QuickNode, Infura, Helius, Bitquery, Blockdaemon, GetBlock), indexers (The Graph, Goldsky, SubQuery, Substreams), chain-specific firehoses (Solana Yellowstone gRPC, Ethereum Geyser-style). Most modern stacks are Kafka-consumer-shaped; beava is HTTP/TCP-push-shaped which is unusual but well-fit to a thin 'node firehose → beava TCP' sidecar. Third-party risk labels: Chainalysis KYT webhook, TRM Labs BLOCKINT API + webhook, Elliptic Holistic API, Merkle Science, Crystal, Scorechain. Sanctions: OFAC SDN list (CSV/JSON, daily), EU consolidated list, UK OFSI, UN. Off-chain: exchange's order-management system event bus (Kafka), KYC service (Sumsub, Persona, Onfido, Jumio). Outbound to the compliance / fraud-rules-engine / case-management UI via batch_get HTTP. gRPC support would close a gap with Tecton/Chalk and help on-chain teams that standardise on gRPC. The natural integration is either (a) thin Kafka-to-beava-TCP sidecar that translates the node firehose into beava push events, or (b) direct ingestion from the exchange's trade/payment event bus.
competition.scoring_engine_coupling: Both. Crypto compliance / risk stacks always run rules-and-ML in parallel: rule engines (vendor DSLs inside TRM/Chainalysis/Elliptic, no-code engines in Unit21/Sardine/Hawk/Flagright, Drools / OpenRules / FEEL in custom builds) on top of features, and ML scorers (XGBoost / LightGBM / ONNX / isolation-forest classifiers, GNN-based illicit-cluster detectors as published on the Elliptic dataset). Beava is feature-serving only; the buyer plugs it into both pipelines.

adoption_signals.existing_public_users_or_case_studies: No public beava crypto / web3 case study at time of research. Comparable platforms with named public users: Chainalysis at 9 of top-10 crypto exchanges; TRM Labs at Coinbase, MoonPay, Visa, Mastercard, American Express (Series B investors), public-sector (DOJ, FBI, IRS-CI, HSI); Elliptic at Standard Chartered, ING, Revolut; Sardine at Uphold, FTX-era stablecoin orgs; Unit21 at Uphold (public case study); Solidus Labs HALO at BitMEX; MetaMask + Phantom integrate Blockaid as default security provider; Coinbase International Exchange built ultra-low-latency on AWS (100,000 msg/s core capability); VeloDB / Apache Doris powers a 'top crypto exchange' real-time analytics for 80M+ users (Medium case study). Open-source AML projects (Jube, Marble) cite production deployments but rarely name customers. [uncertain] — exact named exchange deployments and per-buyer scale figures are not independently verified.

adoption_signals.adversarial_pressure_level: Very high. The adversary set includes state-actor laundering (Lazarus Group, $1.5B Bybit hack Feb 2025, Tornado-Cash + Sinbad usage), professional money-mules at scale, peel-chain and mixer-based laundering automated end-to-end, MEV-aware wash-traders evading market-abuse detection, scam-token deployers spawning thousands of new contracts daily, and well-funded sanctions-evasion infrastructure (Garantex, Bitzlato historical). Feature drift is fast (weeks for mixer-rotation, days for new scam-token patterns). The adversary iterates faster than in bank AML and slower only than payments-fraud and anti-cheat. Net: adversarial pressure is among the highest of any beava use case.

risk_and_non_goals.non_goals: 1) Long-term archive of raw on-chain transactions — buy from Allium, Dune, Footprint, Coin Metrics, Bitquery, Goldsky, or store in Snowflake / Databricks / BigQuery. 2) Historical multi-year batch backfill of all-chain history for cluster discovery — Spark / Flink batch territory, plus the third-party intelligence vendor's own labelling. 3) Address-clustering and entity-resolution at on-chain scale — owned by Chainalysis / TRM / Elliptic / Merkle Science; beava consumes their cluster labels. 4) Graph / hop-distance computation across the full transaction graph — a true graph database (Neo4j, TigerGraph, custom in-house property-graph) or the third-party API does this; beava caches the result. 5) Sanctions-list maintenance and PEP / adverse-media lookups — buy from OFAC feeds, Castellum.AI, ComplyAdvantage, World-Check, Dow Jones. 6) Travel-Rule originator/beneficiary messaging — Notabene, 21 Analytics, Sumsub, Veriscope, Shyft. 7) Case-management UI, alert disposition, SAR narrative generation, regulator e-filing — Unit21, Sardine, Hawk, Lucinity, vendor's own case manager. 8) On-chain node operation and mempool ingestion — Alchemy, QuickNode, Infura, Helius, Bitquery; beava is downstream of the firehose. 9) Model training, model registry, model validation — SageMaker / Vertex / Databricks / MLflow. 10) KYC / sanctions screening of the human customer — Sumsub, Persona, Onfido, Jumio. 11) Trade-surveillance market-abuse typologies (wash trade, spoofing, layering on order book) — Solidus Labs HALO, Nasdaq SMARTS-CCM.
risk_and_non_goals.open_engineering_gaps: To be production-grade for any regulated crypto buyer, beava would need (roughly decreasing priority): (1) TLS termination (mTLS preferred) — non-negotiable; (2) authn/authz with RBAC and per-tenant namespaces (OIDC/SAML for admin); (3) per-read audit log (who-asked-what-when) — directly required for MiCA / FATF reproducibility; (4) point-in-time / as-of feature reads ('what was min_hop_to_OFAC for address X at 14:32:07Z on 2026-02-14?') — directly required for SAR / Travel-Rule reproducibility; (5) in-process sharding or a documented horizontal-scale story (consistent-hash router, replication, failover) — essential given 100M–1B+ address-grain cardinality; (6) hot-standby / synchronous-WAL replication; (7) per-feature TTL and tiered storage (RAM → local SSD) so 90–365-day baselines can outlive RAM at exchange scale; (8) idempotency tokens keyed on (tx_hash, log_index, chain_id) and end_to_end_id for off-chain — required for chain re-orgs and at-least-once node-firehose delivery; (9) chain re-org / tombstone / compensating-write semantics — a correctness-critical addition unique to this domain; (10) triggers / 'fire-on-threshold-cross' webhooks so the feature server can emit alerts directly into the case-management UI ('fire when min_hop_to_OFAC <= 1' or 'sum(outbound_to_mixer, 24h) > $10k'); (11) native graph primitive or first-class integration for hop-distance / cluster-membership cached lookups; (12) native sanctions / mixer / scam-list lookup hook that auto-refreshes on OFAC SDN update; (13) gRPC surface in addition to HTTP/TCP; (14) multi-tenancy so wallet providers and regtech vendors can embed beava across many customer tenants; (15) data-residency controls (EU-only RAM, US-only RAM) for MiCA / GDPR; (16) Kafka-consumer source/sink connector; (17) chain-firehose adapter library for Ethereum/Bitcoin/Solana/Polygon/Tron RPC; (18) Prometheus + OpenTelemetry exporters; (19) GDPR right-to-erasure surface (delete-by-customer-id) that does not corrupt aggregate counters — doubly hard here because on-chain data itself is immutable; (20) deterministic replay from WAL with verifiable hashes.
risk_and_non_goals.trigger_action_required: Yes, very strongly. Wallet-providers and DeFi protocols want signing-modal warnings emitted in <100 ms; exchanges want auto-hold on withdrawal when min_hop_to_OFAC <= 1 or when sum(outbound_to_mixer, 24h) crosses threshold; compliance teams want auto-create-case in Unit21/Sardine/HALO. Beava today is feature-serving only, so the caller's rule engine has to poll-and-threshold. Adding a trigger / webhook surface (or a 'fire when atomic counter crosses threshold' primitive) is one of the two highest-leverage adds for this domain, alongside TLS+authn.
